main_question: Can a physics-informed neural network estimate the transmission rate of an SIR model from noisy case data?
structure: Definitions of the model and the inverse problem support a PINN method, whose result is good for constant beta but limited by collocation-only enforcement and identifiability, leading to an open question about networks.

atoms.title: The SIR model splits a population into three compartments
atoms.statement: The SIR model divides a closed population of size $N$ into susceptible $S(t)$, infected $I(t)$ and recovered $R(t)$ individuals, with $\dot S = -\beta S I/N$, $\dot I = \beta S I/N - \gamma I$, $\dot R = \gamma I$, where $\beta$ is the transmission rate and $\gamma$ the recovery rate.
atoms.evidence: The SIR model divides a closed population of size N into susceptible, infected and recovered individuals

atoms.title: Estimating SIR rates from case data is an inverse problem
atoms.statement: Estimating the transmission rate $\beta$ and recovery rate $\gamma$ of an SIR model from observed case counts is an inverse problem, and it can be ill-posed because different parameter values may produce nearly the same observed curve.
atoms.evidence: Estimating model coefficients from observations of the solution is an inverse problem, and it is often ill-posed

atoms.title: A PINN treats the transmission rate as a trainable parameter
atoms.statement: A physics-informed neural network approximates $(S, I, R)$ with a network $u_\theta(t)$ and learns $\beta$ jointly with $\theta$ by minimising $\mathcal{L} = \mathcal{L}_{\text{data}} + \lambda_r \mathcal{L}_{\text{res}} + \lambda_0 \mathcal{L}_{\text{IC}}$, where $\mathcal{L}_{\text{res}}$ is the mean squared ODE residual at collocation points.
atoms.evidence: treats beta (and possibly gamma) as additional trainable parameters

atoms.title: PINNs recover a constant transmission rate from sparse noisy data
atoms.statement: In a synthetic SIR experiment ($N = 10^5$, $\beta = 0.3$, $\gamma = 0.1$ per day) a PINN recovered $\beta$ within 5% of its true value from 20 observations of $I(t)$ with 10% multiplicative noise.
atoms.evidence: the PINN recovered beta within 5% of its true value from 20 noisy observations

atoms.title: Reporting rate and initial infections are not jointly identifiable
atoms.statement: When only reported cases $\rho I(t)$ are observed with an unknown reporting fraction $\rho$, early-epidemic data cannot separate $\rho$ from the initial number of infected individuals $I(0)$.
atoms.evidence: the reporting fraction and the initial number of infected individuals cannot be separated from early-epidemic data

atoms.title: PINN residuals are enforced only at collocation points
atoms.statement: The physics loss of a PINN penalises the ODE residual only at a finite set of collocation points $\{t_k\}_{k=1}^K$, so a small training loss does not guarantee that the residual vanishes on the whole time interval.
atoms.evidence: The physics loss is only enforced at the collocation points

atoms.title: Can PINNs estimate spatially varying transmission on contact networks?
atoms.statement: Can the PINN approach be extended to metapopulation models on a contact network, where each node $i$ has its own transmission rate $\beta_i$ and nodes are coupled through the graph Laplacian?
atoms.evidence: Can the approach be extended to metapopulation models on a contact network
